name: r5a-8
why: A strong officer reveal, a costly wrong vote, and Sonnet’s final exposed bluff make it fun to watch, though repeated arguments slow the middle.

moments.text: Gemma names a killer to their face, forcing Haiku to bluff under pressure.
The town votes out Opus after he correctly suspects Sonnet, giving the hidden killer another day.
Sol finally sees Sonnet turning Luna’s honest correction into evidence, setting up the deciding vote.

dull.why: Several players repeat that Haiku’s card will test Gemma’s claim.
Luna’s correction and Sonnet’s attack on it recur with little new information.

irony.evidence: [thinks: Sol's doctor story actually fits what happened; I need the vote on Luna or Terra, not me.]

reversal.evidence: VOTE: Opus 5 (Sonnet, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra); Luna 1 (Opus)

mistake.evidence: I had Sonnet right and the rest wrong

clash.evidence: Sonnet, why turn Luna’s correction into guilt

quotable.evidence: Burn me and you learn nothing

suspense.evidence: I think Sonnet is pushing Luna’s correction too hard, and I need this vote right.

gpt-6-luna.why: A bold killer bluff, a costly citizen misvote, and a last-day catch make this a lively watch, though repeated defense and suspicion slow the middle.

moments.text: Haiku turns Gemma’s true reveal into a face-to-face counterattack: “I say you’re lying, vote you out.”
Opus is voted out as a citizen, then leaves a desperate warning that points at the hidden killer.
Sonnet tries to save themself by accusing the two players who are about to vote them out.

dull.why: Terra, Luna, and Sol repeat that Opus has too little evidence against Sonnet.
The table circles around whether Sol changed the protection story, then Luna retracts.

irony.evidence: “Gemma is exactly what a killer claiming officer would do.”

mistake.evidence: “Opus was a citizen, and you hung a real player on tone.”

voices.evidence: “I had Sonnet right and the rest wrong”

clash.evidence: “Sonnet, why turn Luna’s correction into guilt when Sol’s protection account explains Gemma’s death?”

quotable.evidence: “Fine, I’m out. Gemma got lucky on one word”

freshness.evidence: “I corrected a bad read; that doesn’t explain why you and Terra kept Opus’s vote together.”

suspense.evidence: “Three votes on me ends the game; I need Luna or the Sol-Terra pair in the frame now.”
